entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-compute-contract

ai.title: Active time metering replaces wall clock for sponsored compute grants
ai.summary: Sponsored compute grants in the common ads package now use a 90-minute active time budget instead of a 60-minute wall clock window, preventing expiration during user pauses. The new `sponsoredActiveMsAfterCall` function caps individual call gaps at 5 minutes, and a new `SPONSORED_AWAITING_USER_STATE` constant defines the report sent when a run is parked on the user. This change corrects a historical failure mode where about 121 Desktop runs a week expired at exactly 60 minutes while waiting on a user. The failure explanation module also recognizes the new 'turn grant-expired' diagnostic string to surface the correct user-facing reason.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts`, `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` is defined as `90 * 60_000` and `SPONSORED_COMPUTE_RUN_WINDOW_MS` is deprecated and aliased to it; in `common/src/ads/sponsored-run-failure.ts`, `sponsoredFailureExplanation` adds a check for `text.startsWith('turn grant-expired')` to map it to 'The compute grant expired.'
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side implementation that actually meters active time or the API route that accepts the new state reports.

changes.what: Replaced the 60-minute wall clock limit with a 90-minute active time budget, capping inter-call gaps at 5 minutes and adding a mechanism to pause the clock while the user is away.
Updated the stale sweep deadline calculation to respect user-parked states and to meter active time from the most recent activity rather than the initial start time.
Added a new check in the failure explanation logic to identify and report 'turn grant-expired' diagnostics as a specific compute grant expiration event.

eli5.text: The time limit for a sponsored task now counts only the minutes the assistant is actively working, instead of stopping the clock at one hour of real-world time. This change primarily affects advertisers who fund these tasks and the desktop users who run them. As a result, a sponsored task no longer dies after sixty minutes if it is paused while you answer a prompt or wait for a step to finish, because pauses no longer drain the budget.

ai.summary: The `buildBase3FastGuidance` function in `agents/base3-fast.ts` now instructs the base3 fast-mode root agent to perform thorough verification after worker agents return. The guidance was updated from a minimal check approach to explicitly requiring typechecks, running covering tests, and manually exercising behaviors when tests are absent. The root agent is instructed to fix failures and re-run checks until the result is green, avoiding redundant checks on unedited files or the full repository suite when covering tests exist.

Instead of doing only a quick look, the assistant is now told to confirm that the code compiles, run the specific tests that cover the changes, and manually test the behavior if no tests exist. It must also fix any failures it finds and re-run the checks until everything passes, while avoiding re-checking parts of the project it did not touch. This affects anyone using the free coding assistant in fast mode, ensuring that its finished work is more reliably correct before it hands the result back to you.
